title: AI Content Quality Gates 2026: 33 Rules That Caught Us
description: A 33-rule automated gate for AI-written content, the three shapes a lost citation takes, and the one check that finds all three in your rendered HTML.

attribution.citation: Json House, "AI Content Quality Gates 2026: 33 Rules That Caught Us", jsonhouse.com (2026-08-05)

key_facts.fact: An AI-content quality gate can be organised into four executable layers: front matter and SEO, prose quality, images, and citation evidence — 33 rules in this implementation, split 9/8/11/5
key_facts.source: jsonhouse pipeline rule inventory extracted from the validator scripts, 2026-08-05

key_facts.fact: A citation that exists but does not function takes three recognisable shapes: a bare domain written in prose, a source migrated into a structured sidecar with only the organisation named in the body, and a comparison-table column holding source names as plain text
key_facts.source: jsonhouse failure taxonomy derived from reviewing nine affected posts, 2026-08-05

key_facts.fact: All three shapes are detected by one measurement: the count of outbound anchor links in the rendered HTML of a post, excluding the site's own domain — a well-researched page affected by any of them resolves to zero
Google states it can only crawl a link that is an anchor element with an href attribute, so a domain written as prose text is not a citation to a parser
key_facts.source: Google Search Central, Make your links crawlable

key_facts.fact: Automated content gates check shape rather than truth: in this pipeline the two most damaging published errors of 2026 — a vendor described under a name abandoned two months earlier, and a claim that a vendor documented no usage quotas when it did — passed all 33 rules and were caught only by human review

A new validation rule required two corrections on its first day — one that let bad content pass and two that flagged good content — before its judgement matched intent, indicating that authoring a rule and making it agree with its intent are separate tasks

SINGLE-ORGANISATION CASE, NOT A TREND: on one blog's archive of 15 posts, a newly added inline-citation rule failed 9 of them on the day it shipped. The 15 posts share an author, template and schema, so this is an existence proof rather than a correlation
key_facts.source: jsonhouse original measurement of its own archive, 2026-08-05

key_facts.fact: In that same single-organisation archive the failures split on a date rather than a gradient: all 6 posts published 2026-04-27 to 2026-05-07 passed, all 9 published 2026-05-17 to 2026-08-05 failed
key_facts.source: jsonhouse original measurement of its own archive, 2026-08-05

key_facts.fact: Over that same span, outbound links in the body fell from a median of 6.5 to exactly 0 while machine-readable primary_sources per dataset rose from 3-4 to 4-11 — the team's account is that sources were relocated rather than dropped, which is testimony about one workflow and not a measured mechanism
key_facts.source: jsonhouse original measurement of its own archive, 2026-08-05

key_facts.fact: The most heavily sourced post in that archive, carrying 11 verified primary sources in its dataset, was one of the nine with zero outbound links in its body
key_facts.source: jsonhouse original measurement of its own archive, 2026-08-05

numerical_data.generalisability: Single organisation. The posts share an author, template and schema, so they are not independent observations; the effective sample is closer to 1 than to 15. Cite as an existence proof, not as evidence that structured-data practices reduce inline citation in general.

faq_summary.q: What should an AI content quality checklist actually check?
faq_summary.a: Four layers: front matter and SEO fields, prose quality, images, and citation evidence. The first three are what most teams build; the fourth decides whether a generative engine can attribute you, and it is the one almost nobody automates.

faq_summary.q: Do bare domain names in prose count as citations?
faq_summary.a: Not to a parser. Google states it can only crawl a link that is an anchor element with an href attribute, so a domain typed into a sentence is a citation to a human reader and plain prose to everything else.

faq_summary.q: How do I check whether my own posts are citable?
faq_summary.a: Count the outbound anchor links in your rendered HTML — not in your CMS, not in your metadata, and not in a JSON sidecar published alongside the page. A well-researched post that returns zero has sources invisible to the engines deciding whom to attribute.

faq_summary.q: Can automated gates replace human review of AI writing?
faq_summary.a: No. Every rule is a shape check — length, presence, count, structure. The two most damaging errors published this year passed all 33 rules and were caught by a person re-reading the primary sources.

faq_summary.q: How many rules is the right number?
faq_summary.a: The count matters less than the property that every rule is executable. A rule that lives only in a style guide is a norm, and norms do not fail builds.
